intro: To use Read Aloud in Word on Mac, open your document, go to the Review tab, and click Read Aloud. Press Play to hear the text, then use Pause, Previous, Next or Stop to control it.
tldr: Open the Review tab in Word for Mac, then click Read Aloud.
Microsoft lists ⌃⌥Space to start Read Aloud and ⌥Space to play or pause it.
Select text first if you want to hear only part of a document.
The gear icon holds the Reading speed slider and Voice Selection.
If the button is missing, check your Microsoft 365 sign-in and restart Word.

blocks.text: Read Aloud is the fastest way to hear a Word document without printing it or reading every line again. Your ears catch errors your eyes slide past. This guide covers the menu paths, the shortcuts Microsoft lists for Mac, the settings you can change, and the fixes for a button that will not appear.
What you need before you start Read Aloud

Read Aloud is a subscriber feature. Microsoft says it works in Office 2019, Office 2021 and Microsoft 365, and calls it subscriber-only. Microsoft's Immersive Reader page also lists Word 2024, so the version list is not fully consistent across Microsoft's own pages.
Check your version before you hunt through menus. Open Word, choose Word > About Word, and read the version shown. If your copy is older than the versions Microsoft names, the button may be missing.

Voices come from built-in device software or a Microsoft service, so the voice list can differ from one Mac to the next. Neural voices need a stable internet connection and a Microsoft 365 sign-in. If the voice you want is missing, check those two things first.
Find Read Aloud on Word for Mac
Microsoft's Listen to your Word documents page puts Read Aloud on the Review tab for Mac. Click Review in the ribbon at the top of the window, then look for Read Aloud in that tab.

Microsoft's Use Immersive Reader in Word page gives a different route for macOS: View > Learning Tools > Read Aloud. That page lists no Mac shortcuts. The two pages disagree, so check both tabs in your copy. The one that shows Read Aloud is the right route for your build.

blocks.title: Two routes, one button
blocks.text: Microsoft gives Review for Mac on one page and View > Learning Tools on another. Check Review first, then View. Your build decides which route shows the button.

blocks.caption: The two Microsoft pages disagree on the Mac menu path and the shortcuts.

blocks.text: Play, pause and skip through the text

The player has five controls: Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Stop. Stop appears as an x. Play and Pause do what they say. Previous and Next move you through the text, so you can skip past a section you have already checked.

Keys make this faster. On Mac, Option + up arrow skips to the start of the previous paragraph. Option + down arrow skips forward to the next paragraph. When you hear a mistake, use Option + up arrow to jump back and hear that sentence again.

Start Read Aloud with Control + Option + Space, shown here as ⌃⌥Space. Once it runs, Option + Space plays or pauses. Microsoft lists both keys for Mac, but its other page lists no Mac shortcuts, so test them before you rely on them.

blocks.title: Test the keys first
blocks.text: If a shortcut does nothing, that does not mean you pressed it wrong. Use the player buttons while you find out which keys work on your build.
Change the reading speed and voice

Click the gear icon in the Read Aloud player. It opens two settings. The Reading speed slider sets the pace, and Voice Selection lets you pick a different voice. Slow down when you need to hear each word. Speed up once you know the text well.
Read Aloud uses the document's proofing language. If a paragraph is set to French and you hear an English voice, the speech may sound wrong. Check the language of the text before you blame the voice.
Read only part of a document

Select the text first. Then start Read Aloud from the Review tab, with its shortcut, or with the Play control. Microsoft describes this selection method for reading part of a document, so use it whenever only one section needs checking.

Here is a real case. You wrote a long report, and only the summary needs a final pass. Select the summary, start Read Aloud, and listen. You skip the methods and the appendix entirely, which keeps your attention on the part that changed.
Use Read Aloud to proofread your writing

Reading aloud is a known way to catch mistakes. The Learning Scientists summarize a 2022 study by Cushing and Bodner. Their summary says reading aloud gave better proofreading than reading silently or in a disfluent font. The summary gives no effect sizes, so treat it as a useful signal rather than a precise number.

Try this routine. Listen to one section at a time. Pause when a word feels wrong, fix it, then press Play again. Keep a short list of the errors you fix. The list shows which mistakes you make most, so you can check for them first next time.

Text-to-speech matters for people who find reading hard. Dyslexia is common, but estimates vary. The British Dyslexia Association states that 10% of the UK population is dyslexic, with 4% severely affected. Dyslexia Action says the source of that figure is hard to trace, and other estimates range from 3 to 5% up to 20%.
When Read Aloud is missing or greyed out
Start with your sign-in. Confirm you are signed in to your Microsoft 365 account. Then restart Word, or sign out and sign back in. Microsoft lists these two steps for a missing Read Aloud option.

Search results contain many fixes for a greyed-out button, and not all of them apply to a Mac. A Microsoft Q&A community answer gives Option + Esc as the default macOS key for speaking selected text. That is a community answer, not an official Microsoft step. A popular answer in a greyed-out thread tells you to add the Speak command to the Quick Access Toolbar. That thread is about Windows and dates from 2018, so skip it on a Mac.
Read text in other Mac apps with Speech

Word's Read Aloud works inside Word. For other apps, the macOS Speech setting can speak selected text when you press a key. Microsoft's page gives this route: Apple menu > System Preferences > Accessibility > Speech. Turn on Speak selected text when the key is pressed.

In the same pane you can change the key, the system voice and the speaking rate. Microsoft's page says System Preferences. Newer macOS releases may label it System Settings, so look for the Speech options under Accessibility if the name differs.
Mistakes people make with Read Aloud

items: Looking on one tab only. Check Review, then View > Learning Tools.
Starting with nothing selected when only one paragraph needs checking.
Trusting a shortcut before you test it on your build.
Skipping the Microsoft 365 sign-in check when the button is missing.
Following a Windows fix from a greyed-out thread.
Blaming the voice when the proofing language is wrong.

blocks.text: Privacy: what Read Aloud sends and stores

Microsoft says Read Aloud does not store your content or audio data. Voices from a Microsoft service need a sign-in and a stable internet connection. If the document is sensitive, check your organization's policy before you use those voices, and read Microsoft's privacy terms for your account.
Where to go next in Word

Hearing a mistake is only half the job. You still need to mark it or fix it. The guide on [adding a comment in Word on Mac](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-word) shows how to leave a note on the exact spot, so the next editor sees it.

If you want to compare your edits with the original, [Track Changes on Mac](/how-to/turn-on-track-changes-in-word) keeps a record. For a final length check, [see the word count in Word on Mac](/how-to/see-word-count-in-word) before you send the file.

faq.question: Do I need a Microsoft 365 subscription for Read Aloud in Word on Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft calls Read Aloud a subscriber-only feature. Its Listen page names Office 2019, Office 2021 and Microsoft 365. Its Immersive Reader page also lists Word 2024. If your copy is older than those, check the version under Word > About Word.

faq.question: Which keyboard shortcut starts Read Aloud in Word on Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft lists Control + Option + Space, shown as ⌃⌥Space, to start Read Aloud. Option + Space plays or pauses it. The Immersive Reader page lists no Mac shortcuts, so test the keys on your build before you depend on them.

faq.question: Can Read Aloud read one paragraph and then stop?
faq.answer: Yes. Select that paragraph before you start Read Aloud. Then press Play or use the shortcut, and click Stop when the paragraph ends. Microsoft describes selecting text first as the way to read part of a document.

faq.question: Why do Microsoft's pages give different menu paths for Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Listen to your Word documents page says Review for Mac. Its Use Immersive Reader in Word page says View > Learning Tools > Read Aloud on macOS. The pages do not say which build each path covers, so check both tabs in your copy.

faq.question: Does Word store the text or audio that Read Aloud uses?
faq.answer: Microsoft says Read Aloud does not store your content or audio data. Voices from a Microsoft service need a Microsoft 365 sign-in and a stable internet connection. For sensitive documents, check your organization's policy first.

faq.question: How do I change the speed or the voice in Read Aloud?
faq.answer: Click the gear icon in the Read Aloud player. The Reading speed slider sets the pace, and Voice Selection lets you choose a voice. Available voices vary, because they come from built-in device software or a Microsoft service.

faq.question: How do I use Read Aloud in Word for the web or Word for iPad?
faq.answer: In Word for the web, select View, then Immersive reader, and press Play. Exit with the back arrow or Esc. In Word for iPad, go to View > Immersive Reader > Read Aloud, and close it with X.

faq.question: Can I use Read Aloud for text in Mail or on a web page?
faq.answer: Not with Word's Read Aloud. The macOS Speech setting can speak selected text in other apps when you press a key you choose. Microsoft's page gives the route as Apple menu > System Preferences > Accessibility > Speech.

steps.name: Open your document in Word
steps.text: Open the Word file in Word for Mac. Check that the text you want to hear is typed in the document and that you can select it with your mouse or trackpad.

steps.name: Select the text to hear (optional)
steps.text: To hear only part of the document, select that text now. Read Aloud reads your selection instead of the whole file.

steps.name: Open the Review tab
steps.text: Click Review in the ribbon at the top of the Word window. Microsoft's Listen page places Read Aloud here for Mac.

steps.name: Click Read Aloud
steps.text: Click Read Aloud on the Review tab. The Read Aloud player appears with Play, Pause, Previous, Next and Stop (x) controls.
steps.tip: If you do not see Read Aloud here, open View > Learning Tools > Read Aloud. Your build decides which route shows it.

steps.name: Press Play
steps.text: Click Play in the player. Word reads the text out loud. Once it runs, Option + Space plays or pauses it.

steps.name: Move between paragraphs
steps.text: Use Previous and Next in the player to move through the text. Option + up arrow goes to the start of the previous paragraph, and Option + down arrow skips to the next one.

steps.name: Change the reading speed
steps.text: Click the gear icon in the player. Drag the Reading speed slider until the pace suits you.

steps.name: Pick a voice
steps.text: In the same gear menu, open Voice Selection and choose a voice. Neural voices need a stable internet connection and a Microsoft 365 sign-in.

steps.name: Stop when you finish
steps.text: Click Stop, shown as an x, to end Read Aloud. Read Aloud only reads the text. It does not edit the file.

troubleshooting.problem: Read Aloud is not on the Review tab
troubleshooting.fix: Check View > Learning Tools > Read Aloud. Microsoft's Immersive Reader page gives that route for macOS. Use whichever route shows the button in your copy.

troubleshooting.problem: Read Aloud is missing or greyed out
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm you are signed in to your Microsoft 365 account. Then restart Word, or sign out and sign back in. Skip the Windows-only Speak command fix from the older Q&A thread.
Microsoft lists ⌃⌥Space and ⌥Space for Mac, but its Immersive Reader page lists no Mac shortcuts. Use the player buttons while you find out which keys work on your build.

troubleshooting.problem: The voice you want is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Available voices depend on built-in device software or a Microsoft service. Neural voices need a stable internet connection and a Microsoft 365 sign-in.

troubleshooting.problem: The speech sounds wrong for the text
troubleshooting.fix: Read Aloud uses the document's proofing language. Check the language of the text, then start Read Aloud again.
